# E127 -- Dow Jones

## Metadata
- **Brand**: Dow Jones Enterprise Media Group
- **Industry**: Media / Financial Information / News
- **Document**: Brand Manual & Design Guidelines
- **Year**: 2008 (March 14, 2008)
- **Pages**: 65
- **Designer/Agency**: Not credited (created in Adobe InDesign CS3; likely internal or agency-led rebrand)

## Brand Strategy
- **Goal**: Develop a new communications framework and visual identity system unifying the entire Dow Jones Enterprise Media Group across all sub-brands, sectors, and products.
- **Problem statement**: Over time, collateral had fragmented into multiple styles, logos, graphic treatments, and tones of voice -- "complicated and confusing, for us as well as our audience."
- **Brand values**: Credibility, respect, accuracy, authority.
- **Design principles**: "Simple and unified. Robust and flexible. Clear and consistent."
- **Scope**: Governs all communications, internally and externally, across all media.

## Logo
- **Wordmark**: "DOW JONES" in uppercase, bold, condensed serif/slab typeface with a distinctive italic lean. Features a horizontal swoosh/underline extending from the right side of the wordmark.
- **Presentation**: Logo appears on cover at bottom-left on blue grid paper background, reinforcing precision and data-driven identity.
- **Sub-brand**: Specifically the "Enterprise Media Group" division of Dow Jones.

## Typography
- **Observable**: Clean serif body text throughout the guidelines document itself. Headers in a bold sans-serif or semi-serif. Body copy is well-set with generous line spacing.
- **Detailed specs**: Not captured in sampled pages (likely covered in dedicated typography section elsewhere in the 65-page document).

## Color
- **Primary blue**: A medium-bright blue used for the grid motif, section dividers, and accent text (appears to be a Dow Jones brand blue, ~#0066B2 or similar).
- **Warm neutral**: Warm beige/greige (#E8E0D8 or similar) used for content page backgrounds.
- **Section divider**: Page 13 introduces "Color palette print / Color palette web / Color palette examples" -- dedicated color section follows.
- **Text colours**: Dark brown/charcoal for body text on neutral backgrounds; blue for accent/highlight text.

## Graphics
- **Grid motif**: Blue graph-paper grid used as a recurring design device (cover and section dividers), evoking financial data, precision, and analytical rigour.
- **Layout**: Generous whitespace, structured asymmetric layouts with left-column navigation labels and right-column content.
- **Page numbering**: Paired numbers (08/09, 10/11, 20/21) suggesting spread-based design.

## Photography
- Not directly observed in sampled pages.

## Applications
- Not directly observed in sampled pages; the 65-page depth suggests application examples exist later in the document.

## Tone of Voice
- **Brand language section** (page 12, titled "Tone of voice / Brand language"):
- **Philosophy**: "Dow Jones Enterprise Media Group is an organization founded on the power of the written word." The brand stands for authority, integrity, accuracy, and quality.
- **Approach**: Writing should be "as instantly recognizable as our logo or our color palette" across all media -- print, web, advertising, multi-media, exhibitions.
- **Style**: Compelling and engaging, straightforward and easy to digest. No jargon, no technicalities. "As accessible as it is convincing."
- **We are / We are not** pairings (10 pairs):
  - Authoritative / Not arrogant
  - Compelling / Not dramatic
  - Persuasive / Do not coerce
  - Avoid jargon / Do not oversimplify
  - Consistent / Not repetitive
  - Explain / Do not condescend
  - Concise / Never short
  - Write in-depth / Never bore
  - Vary our pace / Do not change tone
  - Dynamic / Not aggressive

## Outliers
- Notably early document (2008) for an enterprise media brand -- pre-dates many modern brand guideline conventions.
- The blue grid paper motif is a distinctive and memorable design choice, directly referencing financial/analytical heritage.
- The "We are / We are not" tone of voice framework is exceptionally well-articulated with 10 paired contrasts -- unusually thorough for the era.
- Addresses the challenge of unifying a fragmented multi-brand portfolio under one visual identity system.

## Quality Score
- **3/5** -- Solid foundational brand manual with particularly strong tone-of-voice articulation. The grid paper design device is distinctive. However, the document is from 2008 and likely reflects pre-digital-era design thinking. Sparse visual examples in sampled pages; the minimalist layout borders on under-designed in places (page 2 nearly blank). The 65-page length suggests depth, but core visual specs (typography, full color palette) were not captured in sampled pages.
